subject.title: Cron sessions deliver hallucinated output instead of failing cleanly when tool calls fail

question: What should OpenClaw do by default for cron or unattended final assistant text when the same run recorded failed tools, missing required data, or no proof of the claimed side effect?
rationale: Current behavior intentionally balances final-text recovery, warning suppression, plugin hooks, and narrow fatal signals; changing it affects security, operator trust, and compatibility for existing cron jobs.

options.title: Define core fail-closed finalization
options.body: Make cron or unattended delivery require structured successful recovery or explicit failure acknowledgement before user-visible final text can be delivered after tool failures.

options.title: Keep generic claim verification plugin-first
options.body: Document that broad success-claim verification belongs in ClawHub/plugins while limiting core to current narrow fatal error and warning behavior.

options.title: Split narrower canonical work
options.body: Keep this issue open for cron fail-closed delivery while tracking fake tool-call syntax and general success-claim verification in related issues.

recommendation.title: Define core fail-closed finalization
recommendation.body: Make cron or unattended delivery require structured successful recovery or explicit failure acknowledgement before user-visible final text can be delivered after tool failures.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a default agent-runtime security and compatibility policy choice, and steipete has the strongest recent source-history signal on the relevant cron and agent-runtime paths.
